summary: Iteration 13 re-tested the fixes for the iteration 12 findings. All requested items pass. Backend: /tmp/iter13/test_iter13.py passed 8/8 against the public URL, and the in-process suite /app/backend/tests passed 111/111. (1) Owner A changing owner B's role (PUT) returns 403 and revoking B (DELETE) returns 403. B's memberships are unchanged. Deactivate and reset-2fa on B also return 403, and B's session stays valid. (2) Deactivate, activate and reset-2fa on the developer return 404, and PUT on the developer's membership returns 404. For a collaborator whose last company access was revoked (no shared company), deactivate, activate and reset-2fa return 404. (3) A company created by A automatically gives B the titolare role (GET /companies/{id} as B shows role=titolare). (4) Accepting an invite as an existing user: 5 mixed failures (wrong password or wrong code) each return 401. The 6th attempt returns 429 even with a valid code, and the normal /auth/login also returns 429. A recovery code in ABCD-EFGH format is accepted in invite-totp-code. The response is 200 with no access_token, and the token is then 404. (5) In the UI, after accepting as an existing user, /login shows the 'existing' notice 'Invito accettato: i nuovi accessi sono già attivi...' and the email is prefilled. (6) The Members 'new invite' link and the developer 'Invito titolare' link both equal window.location.origin + /invito/<token>, and both pages open correctly. (7) The served login bundle contains 0 occurrences of 'titolare@demo.it', 'log del server' and the developer password. The developer password also appears 0 times in the backend logs. (8) Members UI as owner A: all 5 of B's role selects are disabled, and B has no Revoca, Azzera verifica, Disattiva or add-access controls. A collaborator row has enabled selects, Revoca, Azzera verifica and Disattiva, and changing the role via the UI gives the 'Ruolo aggiornato' toast. Regression: developer forced 2FA enrollment in the UI passes. The flow is the setup notice, a wrong code is rejected, 10 codes appear, done stays disabled until the checkbox is ticked, then /sviluppatore. Developer login without a code returns 401 2fa_required and with a code returns 200. GET /api/companies returns [] and /members returns 403. Idle logout (last activity set 16 minutes back) redirects to /login?scaduta=1 with the idle notice.

minor.issue: This does not use _managed_target. An owner can add a membership for any non-owner user id, even one sharing no company, and even a deactivated user. Low risk inside a single group, but it is inconsistent with the deactivate/activate scoping.
For an existing user, this does not check user.active. A deactivated user can accept an invite and gain memberships. They still cannot log in, so the impact is low.

issues: The disabled role selects look almost the same as enabled ones and there is no hint explaining why (e.g. 'Gli accessi di un titolare non si modificano'). Consider a tooltip, a short note or a plain role badge instead of the select.

critical_code_review_comments: The DB was NOT wiped as the context note said. At the start it held iteration 12 test users (test_ownera_fa44f1, test_ownerb_b5b17c, test_collab_610a89) and 3 companies, and the developer already had 2FA enrolled. To test enrollment, the tester reset the developer's 2FA directly in Mongo, then re-enrolled it through the UI.
TOTP secrets are stored in plaintext in users.totp_secret. Consider encrypting them at rest with a key from env.
accept_invite returns different messages for a wrong password and for a wrong code, so it reveals when the password is correct. This is mitigated by the lockout, which counts both.
